name: Ground handling and airport services

problems.words: Airlines deduct SLA penalties and we can't prove whose fault the delay was
quick_ideas: Take last month's penalties and note which had any ramp record at all, so you see how many were unwinnable
Ask supervisors to note the time and reason of every delay this week, so you start building evidence.

workzap_build.text: a phone turnaround log with step times, delay reasons and photos signed by the supervisor, producing an evidence pack per flight for every penalty dispute.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many penalties land in a typical month?
problems.free_stops: Which steps are timed and how the evidence pack is assembled is set out in the solution document.

problems.words: Turnarounds we did don't all make it onto the invoice
quick_ideas: Match one month's flights handled against invoice lines for your biggest airline, so you see the gap
Note where missed ones usually fall (night flights, extra services), so you know where to look.

workzap_build.text: billing reconciliation that compares flights handled with invoices raised per airline every day and flags anything not yet billed.

problems.ask_first: Are your contracts per turnaround, per passenger or monthly fixed?

problems.words: Airlines pay months late and payroll is due every month

workzap_build.text: a receivables tracker per airline with ageing, automatic statement reminders and a view of expected receipts against payroll dates.

never_say: Anything about ramp or airside safety procedures, dangerous goods, aircraft loading, weight and balance, de-icing or security screening.
Any reading of PCAA, GCAA, airport authority or Transport Canada rules.
Help bypassing screening, moving unscreened items or obtaining passes improperly, or any angle on influencing officials in tenders.
Employment-law advice on contract staff; suggest they talk to their lawyer.
Covert investigation of individual staff over baggage theft, and any storage of staff names, pass numbers or passenger details.

sample_reply.person: Airlines keep cutting penalties off our invoices and we never have proof it wasn't us. Can you help?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this is fixable, and it starts with what gets recorded at the time of the delay. 1. Go through last month's penalties and see which had any ramp record at all, so you know how many you could never have won. 2. Ask supervisors to note the time and reason of every delay this week, so evidence starts building straight away. Workzap can do this automatically for you: every turnaround timed step by step on a phone, with photos and the supervisor's sign-off, and an evidence pack ready for each flight an airline disputes. Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
